why_this_paper_was_read: ch19 and ch22 of this book carry a load-bearing datum — MEMIT's zsRE Specificity 26.6 is BELOW the unedited GPT-J's 27.0 [MEMIT Table 1] — and that single number carries much of the Theta-path ceiling argument. This paper mechanises sequential-editing collapse and runs to 20,000 edits, so it is the first corpus-external candidate to make that ceiling conditional. It also supplies, from outside A-group, the rho measurement that ch19 declared absent from every paper in that chapter.

problem_stated.as_the_paper_frames_it: Knowledge edits are not isolated in practice: 'models are updated repeatedly over time, leading to the setting of sequential knowledge editing' [§1, p.1], which 'requires both accurate edits and the preservation of general abilities'. The paper's claim of novelty is not that collapse happens — RECT, PRUNE and AlphaEdit already target it — but that nobody has said WHY: 'A key limitation is that most existing methods primarily mitigate interference across updates through heuristic constraints or regularization ... without explicitly modeling how parameter updates interact with the intrinsic structure of pretrained weights. In particular, they do not clarify which parts of the pretrained weights are most relevant to general abilities, or how repeated updates accumulate and gradually degrade them.' [§1, p.2]
problem_stated.the_operational_question: Three questions, asked in the SVD basis of the FFN weight matrices of LLaMA3-8B: '(i) where a model's general abilities are concentrated within these spectral components, (ii) how sensitive these components are to perturbations, and (iii) how sequential editing progressively distorts these components in practice.' [§2, p.2]
problem_stated.the_answer_asserted: 'sequential editing fails when cumulative update progressively corrupt the dominant singular directions of weight matrices, which are strongly associated with general abilities' [§2, p.2, sic — subject-verb disagreement in the original].
problem_stated.note_writer_remark: [note-writer] Read against this book's frame, the paper's object is NOT a sleep-time procedure. It is the WRITE PRIMITIVE of ch19 placed on a clock and run 200 times, plus a geometric constraint on the update. That placement is exactly what ch11 Table 11-2 says ROME and MEMIT lack ('시계 부재'). See discriminant_verdict.

core_mechanism.one_line_unified: The paper adds no update rule of its own. It takes an existing (U-Theta) write operator — a closed-form MEMIT/AlphaEdit/RECT/PRUNE/NSE update, or a MEND hypernetwork update — and post-multiplies it by a two-sided orthogonal projector that annihilates every component touching the top-k left OR right singular subspace of the current weight matrix, so that $\Delta W_{\mathrm{safe}} = (I - U_k U_k^{\top})\,\Delta W\,(I - V_k V_k^{\top})$.
core_mechanism.the_projector_identity: [note-writer] The paper never writes the projector form. Its Eq. (6) sums $\alpha_{ij} u_i v_j^{\top}$ over $i>k$ AND $j>k$, with $\alpha_{ij}=\langle \Delta W, u_i v_j^{\top}\rangle_F = u_i^{\top}\Delta W v_j$ [§3.1 Eq. (4), §3.2 Eq. (6), App. B Eq. (18)]. Assembling those two facts gives the two-sided projector above. The book must state it in projector form, because that form makes the invariance property (below) visible and the printed form does not.
core_mechanism.the_unproved_load_bearing_fact: [note-writer] The property that actually makes the method work is never stated or proved. If $N = \Delta W_{\mathrm{safe}}$ then $U_k^{\top} N = 0$ and $N V_k = 0$, so $U_k^{\top}(W_0+N) = U_k^{\top} W_0$ and $(W_0+N)V_k = W_0 V_k$: the original top-$k$ singular triplets remain exact singular triplets of the edited matrix, with unchanged singular values, for as long as they remain the top $k$. THIS is why App. G.6 can report max SS = 1 at every round, and why re-running the SVD on the CURRENT matrix (as App. C.6 says the implementation does) recovers the same protected subspace as running it on the original. The paper instead spends a full appendix (App. B, Theorem 1, Eqs. (7)-(18)) proving the trivial fact that $\{u_p v_q^{\top}\}$ is an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ — a statement that holds for ANY two orthonormal bases and has nothing to do with editing.

equations_unified.gloss: The paper's founding move: read a weight slice as a sum of independent rank-one input-output mappings. 'an input vector $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$ is projected onto $v_i$, scaled by $\sigma_i$, and expanded along $u_i$ to produce the output' [§2.1, p.2]. Nothing here is new; what is new is using this basis to score an EDIT.

equations_unified.latex: \widetilde{\Theta}^{(l)}_{n\%} \;=\; \sum_{i\in I}\sigma_i u_i v_i^{\top}, \qquad I = \text{smallest index set with } \textstyle\sum_{i\in I}\sigma_i \ge \tfrac{n}{100}\sum_{i=1}^{r}\sigma_i
equations_unified.gloss: The localisation probe. Reconstruct the matrix from the smallest energy-$n\%$ set and measure GLUE. Answer: $n=5$ recovers ~62.6% of original performance [§2.2, p.3].

The sensitivity probe. Decile groups by cumulative energy; each group's perturbation randomly remaps that group's INPUT directions onto ALL output directions, then is rescaled to a common Frobenius norm 'thereby enabling a fair comparison' [§2.3, p.3]. Symmetric output-side version in App. F.1.

The two degradation instruments. LS is macroscopic — Frobenius cosine between the low-rank reconstructions of the original and round-$k$ matrices. SS is microscopic — cosine between a dominant singular vector of the edited matrix and each original singular vector. Dominant = 'top 10% components by singular value energy' [§2.4, p.3].

outer_vs_inner.reader_takeaway: [note-writer] For the book's reader, the important row is the SVD row. The paper's ONLY per-round cost beyond the base editor is a full SVD of the weight slice plus two dense matrix products, and the paper prices that at +4.05% (GPT-J) / +1.91% (LLaMA3) wall-clock per 100 edits [Table 9, p.19]. That is the cheapest control knob any paper in this corpus has proposed for the Theta path, and it is the reason the paper deserves a reading despite failing the discriminant.

how_this_paper_differs_from_the_canonica: There is no $\eta_\Theta$ and no $\nabla_\Theta$ in the outer update. The base editors are closed-form least-squares solves (MEMIT family) or a hypernetwork (MEND). This is the same deviation ch19 §19.4 already recorded for ROME/MEMIT — the book's (U-Theta) admits non-SGD writes.

$\mathrm{gen}(\cdot;B_s)$ is the IDENTITY. $\mathcal{R}_k$ is 100 triples drawn in order from CounterFact or zsRE. No inference produces the content of the write. This is the condition on which the discriminant turns.

A PROJECTOR is inserted between the update and the parameters. No other paper in the corpus does this. The nearest neighbours are AlphaEdit (project onto the null space of a covariance estimated from 100K external Wikipedia triples) and DeltaEdit (project orthogonal to accumulated past update directions) — both are extrinsic; this one is intrinsic to the pretrained spectrum [App. E, Table 3, p.13].

The round index runs to $k=200$. Every other Theta-path paper in the corpus stops at $k=1$ (ROME, MEMIT, LoRA, Generative Adapter), at a handful (SEAL, LM Need Sleep), or at $k=100$ (Continual Facts). This paper's $k$ is the corpus maximum.
$\mathcal{H}_k$ does not exist. There is no accumulated experience; there is a fixed dataset consumed in order.

C_cap.value: absent as reported; structurally zero for the served artefact and unbounded for the editing procedure
C_cap.detail: The edited model is the same size as the original, so per-fact served state is 0 bytes — the Theta path's defining property (→ ch19, ch22 §22.7). But the METHOD's transient state is never reported: the paper gives no $m$, no $n$, no layer list, no dtype, no SVD memory. [본서 산술] Under the stated implementation ('For SVD computation, we use torch.linalg.svd' [App. C.6, p.14]) and PyTorch's default `full_matrices=True`, a LLaMA3-8B FFN down-projection of shape 4096 × 14336 yields $V\in\mathbb{R}^{14336\times 14336}$ = 2.06e8 elements ≈ 822 MB in fp32, plus $U\in\mathbb{R}^{4096\times4096}$ ≈ 67 MB and a coefficient matrix of 5.87e7 elements ≈ 235 MB — over 1.1 GB of transient working set per edited layer per round. The shapes are this note's assumption, not the paper's statement; the paper never prints a matrix shape. Flagged in todo_verify.

rho.value: PRESENT — and this is the single most valuable thing in the paper for this book
rho.detail: This is the corpus's densest measurement of round-wise degradation for a Theta write primitive. Four independent curves: (a) §2.4 — MEMIT on LLaMA3, 20 rounds × 100 edits on CounterFact, with Efficacy/Paraphrase (Fig. 6) and GLUE F1 (Fig. 7) plotted against edit number: 'both editing performance and general ability remain stable in early rounds but deteriorate rapidly after round 10, collapsing almost entirely by round 20' [§2.4, p.4]. (b) §4.2 / Fig. 9 — GLUE against edit number to 10,000: 'MEMIT and RECT collapse to near-zero performance after only 3,000 edits, and even the more robust ALPHAEDIT eventually suffers a complete collapse after 8,000 edits' [§4.2, p.6]. (c) The protected arm: 'REVIVE enhanced methods maintains an overall average 86.34% of its performance across all tasks after 10,000 edits' [§4.2, p.6]. (d) The spectral proxy: LS drops sharply after ~round 15, SS reaches near-orthogonality by round 20 [§2.4, p.4]; for AlphaEdit, max SS < 0.3 by the end of 10,000 edits [App. F.2, p.17].
rho.what_it_does_NOT_measure: rho of the WRITTEN CONTENT by recency. The paper never reports how edit #1 fares after edit #20,000. Its Efficacy/Paraphrase numbers are aggregates whose evaluation protocol is never stated (see unfavorable_facts). So the quantity ch22 calls 도달 실패 has no number here.
rho.value_for_the_book: ch19 §19.5 prints '논문에 없음. 순차 적응·delta 누적·반복 write 실험이 0건' in the rho cell for all three of its papers. That statement remains true of those papers. But the corpus can now cite a rho curve for MEMIT itself, measured elsewhere: general ability near-zero at 3,000 edits unprotected, 86.34% retained at 10,000 edits protected.

N_q.detail: Global edits, shared weights, no per-query state. The amortisation identity (A) degenerates — one write, unbounded queries, zero marginal read cost. The paper never frames anything as amortisation.

experiments.protocol_gaps_first: No seeds. No variance. No error bars. No confidence intervals. No significance test. Whole-text grep for 'seed', 'variance', 'standard deviation', 'error bar' returns nothing but 'covariance' in three unrelated sentences. Every number below is a single point estimate. The paper also never states whether the reported Efficacy/Paraphrase/Neighborhood after 10,000 or 20,000 edits are computed over ALL edited facts or only over the final round — this is load-bearing and is recorded in unfavorable_facts and todo_verify.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The mechanism claim is associational, and the paper's own hedges say so. §2.4's evidence is temporal co-occurrence between behavioural collapse and spectral drift inside ONE run (LLaMA3, CounterFact, MEMIT, 2,000 edits), replicated once in an appendix (AlphaEdit).
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'closely associated with', 'structurally associated with', 'suggesting a primary mechanism underlying this collapse'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The abstract and §1 promise a mechanism; the diagnosis section delivers a correlation. No experiment induces spectral drift without behavioural collapse or vice versa. The only interventional evidence is that BLOCKING the drift also blocks the collapse (§4.2 + App. G.6), which is consistent with the subspace being a mediator but equally consistent with it being a co-symptom of the same over-large update — a reading the norm-growth result (Table 2) actively supports.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The sensitivity finding of §2.3 is close to definitional. Perturbations are normalised to EQUAL Frobenius norm across energy deciles, then applied to remap that decile's input directions onto random output directions. Damaging the directions that carry most of the matrix's action naturally does most damage.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'These results reveal a paradoxical property: the spectral directions most associated with general abilities are also the most fragile under perturbations.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: There is nothing paradoxical about it, and the design does not distinguish 'this subspace is unusually fragile' from 'this subspace does most of the work'. A control that matched perturbations on induced output change rather than on input norm is absent. The perturbations are also i.i.d. Gaussian, not edit-shaped.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The main text's cross-references to its two central figures are SWAPPED. §2.4 attributes the LS result to 'Figure 4' and the SS result to 'Figure 5', but Figure 4's caption reads 'Singular vector similarity (SS) under sequential editing from rounds 6 to 20' and Figure 5's reads '$LS_t$ from rounds 1 to 20'.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: These are the two instruments the paper's whole diagnosis rests on, and the sentence that states the diagnosis points each one at the other's figure.
unfavorable_facts.source: [§2.4, p.4 vs Figure 4 caption p.4 and Figure 5 caption p.4]

unfavorable_facts.fact: Table 1 and Table 7 disagree at the same nominal configuration. Both report MEMIT+REVIVE at 10,000 sequential CounterFact edits with $\theta_{\mathrm{prot}}=0.10$ (App. C.6 fixes the threshold to 0.10 for the main tables). LLaMA3's CounterFact row matches exactly (95.62 / 84.60 / 62.17 / 603.22 / 29.39), which shows the two tables intend the same setting — but every other cell differs.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The zsRE Neighborhood cell is the one this book most wants to quote, and it appears as both 27.87 and 29.77 for GPT-J and as both 32.01 and 31.88 for LLaMA3. No seeds or variance are reported, so a reader cannot tell whether this is run-to-run noise or two different experiments printed under one label.
unfavorable_facts.source: [Table 1, p.6; Table 4, p.18; Table 7, p.19; App. C.6, p.14]

unfavorable_facts.fact: Table 4 prints IDENTICAL zsRE baseline triples for two different methods: MEMIT on GPT2-XL is 53.00 / 46.27 / 12.76 and AlphaEdit on GPT2-XL is also 53.00 / 46.27 / 12.76.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The duplication is baked into the derived percentages — MEMIT+REVIVE is marked ↑28.7% / ↑31.4% / ↑112.4% and AlphaEdit+REVIVE ↑28.5% / ↑23.5% / ↑59.4%, and both sets recompute correctly against the SAME base. So the improvement figures for AlphaEdit on GPT2-XL/zsRE were computed against a row that is almost certainly MEMIT's.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The sensitivity claim is contradicted by the sensitivity table. §4.2 states 'REVIVE exhibits strong robustness, maintaining high performance across a wide range of $\tau$ values ... stable performance can be achieved without careful hyperparameter tuning.' Table 7 shows a monotone trade-off on all three models.
unfavorable_facts.numbers: Over the swept range $\theta_{\mathrm{prot}}=0.05\to0.30$: LLaMA3 Paraphrase 86.03 → 67.56 while Neighborhood 59.70 → 71.86; GPT-J Paraphrase 83.72 → 64.30 while Neighborhood 57.26 → 74.94; GPT2-XL Efficacy 91.89 → 73.03 and Paraphrase 80.72 → 57.28.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: A 19-point Efficacy swing and a 23-point Paraphrase swing is not insensitivity. What the table actually shows is a clean generalisation-versus-specificity frontier — which is a better result than the one claimed, and the paper describes it as the absence of a trade-off.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The abstract's two claims are measured at different horizons. 'REVIVE consistently improves editing efficacy while substantially preserving general abilities under long-horizon sequential editing, including extreme settings with up to 20,000 edits' [Abstract, p.1]. Every general-ability measurement (Figures 9, 16, 17) stops at 10,000 edits. At 20,000 edits the only non-editing evidence is a t-SNE scatter (Figure 12).
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The 20,000-edit headline and the general-ability claim never meet in the same experiment.
unfavorable_facts.source: [Abstract, p.1; §4.2, p.6; Figure 9, p.6; Figure 10, p.7; Figure 12, p.7; Table 6, p.18]

unfavorable_facts.fact: Table 6 (the 20,000-edit table) contains ONLY REVIVE-enhanced rows. There is no unprotected baseline column and no pre-edit row. The claimed 'average improvements of +75.1% in Efficacy and +53.1% in Fluency' cannot be verified from any table; the baselines exist only as areas in the radar plots of Figure 10.

Specificity is NOT restored at any horizon on the sharper probe, and the paper never compares against its own pre-edit row. CounterFact Neighborhood: LLaMA3 pre-edit 89.73 → 62.17 at 10,000 edits (MEMIT+REVIVE) → 56.90 at 20,000 edits; GPT-J pre-edit 83.50 → 66.52 at 10,000. Losses of 27.56, 32.83 and 16.98 points [본서 산술].
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The paper's headline framing is 'preserving general abilities'. Neighborhood Score IS the locality/specificity axis, it is printed in every table, and it monotonically degrades — but no sentence in the paper compares any Neighborhood value to the pre-edit row that sits at the top of its own Table 1.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The excuse offered for REVIVE's Neighborhood losses does not fit its own strongest counter-example. §4.2 writes 'For certain methods such as NSE, applying REVIVE leads to a moderate decrease in Neighborhood Success. This behavior is likely attributable to the fact that high neighborhood scores can arise trivially when edits fail to modify the model.' But NSE on LLaMA3 at 10,000 edits has Efficacy 77.59 — its edits did not fail — and Neighborhood 86.12, within 3.61 points of the pre-edit 89.73. REVIVE takes that to 65.72.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: On this row NSE alone is the arm that best preserves specificity while still editing, and the paper's stated explanation attributes its score to failure.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Applying REVIVE makes things worse in seven printed cells and the prose says the opposite. App. G.1 states 'Across all evaluated baselines, incorporating REVIVE consistently improves editing performance and stability.' Table 4 shows RECT+REVIVE on GPT2-XL at Efficacy 82.99 (↓4.1%) and Paraphrase 69.20 (↓0.4%). Neighborhood falls for NSE on all three models (↓23.6% / ↓15.1% / ↓7.4%) and Fluency falls in three cells (↓0.1% / ↓0.5% / ↓0.6%).
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: This is the corpus's recurring pattern — a summary sentence that the paper's own table refutes — and it is the third type §6.4 of the book's style rules forbids softening.
unfavorable_facts.source: [App. G.1, p.15; Table 1, p.6; Table 4, p.18]

unfavorable_facts.fact: No seeds, no variance, no confidence intervals, no significance tests anywhere. Whole-text grep for 'seed', 'variance', 'standard deviation', 'error bar', 'significan' returns only 'covariance' (three times, about AlphaEdit) and 'significantly' in prose.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Every claim in the paper is a single point estimate, including the Table 1 vs Table 7 discrepancies above, which cannot therefore be dismissed as noise or attributed to it.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The evaluation protocol for the editing metrics is never stated. Nowhere does the paper say whether Efficacy/Paraphrase/Neighborhood after 10,000 or 20,000 edits are computed over ALL edited facts or only over the most recent round. §2.4 says 'After each editing round, we evaluate...' for the 2,000-edit diagnostic, but §4.2 and Tables 1/4/6 say nothing.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The entire retention reading of the paper turns on this. If the metrics cover all edits, Efficacy 91.94 at 20,000 edits is a strong retention claim; if they cover the last round, it says nothing about whether early edits survive. This book cannot cite the number for retention until it is resolved.
unfavorable_facts.source: [§2.4, p.4; §4.2, p.6; Tables 1, 4, 6 — captions read only 'Performance on sequential editing over 10,000 Samples']

unfavorable_facts.fact: Algorithm 1 as printed is not executable at these scales. Line 3 says 'Construct orthogonal basis $\{u_i v_j^{\top} \mid i=1,\ldots,m;\ j=1,\ldots,n\}$' and lines 4-8 compute $\alpha_{ij}\leftarrow\langle\Delta W, u_i v_j^{\top}\rangle_F$ in a double loop. That is $mn$ matrices of $mn$ entries each — for one LLaMA3 FFN slice, order $10^{15}$ floats — and $O(m^2n^2)$ work.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The measured overhead (Table 9, +4.05% / +1.91%) is only possible under the matrix form $\alpha = U^{\top}\Delta W V$, which the paper never writes. App. B Eq. (18) contains the ingredient ($c_{pq}=u_p^{\top}Xv_q$) but the connection is never made. So the algorithm a reader would implement and the algorithm that produced the numbers are different, and no code is released.
unfavorable_facts.source: [Algorithm 1, App. A, p.10; App. B Eq. (18), p.11; App. G.8 and Table 9, p.19; no code URL anywhere]

unfavorable_facts.fact: The one non-trivial mathematical fact behind the method is unproved, while a trivial one gets a full appendix. App. B proves that outer products of two orthonormal bases form an orthonormal basis of the matrix space — true for any orthonormal bases, and unrelated to editing. The property that actually explains App. G.6's max SS = 1 (that the protected triplets survive the update exactly, since $U_k^{\top}\Delta W_{\mathrm{safe}}=0$ and $\Delta W_{\mathrm{safe}}V_k=0$) is never stated.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Without it, the reader cannot see why re-running SVD on the CURRENT matrix each round (App. C.6) is equivalent to using the ORIGINAL matrix (§3.1, Algorithm 1) — nor when it stops being equivalent, namely when the accumulated complement component grows large enough to reorder the spectrum.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The method's own description contradicts itself on which matrix is decomposed. §3.1 and Algorithm 1 line 2 say the singular basis is that of 'the original weight matrix'; App. C.6 says 'Before each update, we perform SVD on the current parameter matrix'.
unfavorable_facts.source: [§3.1, p.5; Algorithm 1, p.10; App. C.6, p.14]

unfavorable_facts.fact: §3.2 reverses its own input/output convention. §2.1 establishes that an input is projected onto $v_i$ and expanded along $u_i$. §3.2 then writes 'The corresponding singular vectors $\{u_i\}_{i=1}^{k}$ and $\{v_i\}_{i=1}^{k}$ span the dominant input and output subspaces, respectively.'

Even the protected arm accumulates an update larger than half the original matrix. GPT-J Layer 3 Frobenius norm goes 105.51 → 163.47 over 10,000 edits with REVIVE. By the triangle inequality the accumulated safe update has Frobenius norm at least 57.96, i.e. at least 55% of the pretrained matrix's own norm [본서 산술]; the unprotected MEMIT arm reaches at least 20841.15, i.e. at least 197× [본서 산술].
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The paper reads Table 2 as evidence that REVIVE 'substantially constrains and stabilizes this growth', which is true relatively (1.55× vs 198.5×) and understated absolutely. It also means the low-energy directions are absorbing a very large amount of mass, and nothing in the paper asks whether they saturate.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Table 2 is one layer of one model. 'Layer 3' of GPT-J. No other layer, no other model, no distribution across the edited layer set — and the edited layer set is never named.

'Energy' is defined as $\sum_i \sigma_i$, not $\sum_i \sigma_i^2$. The paper never remarks on this. Under the conventional squared definition the same threshold would select a smaller $k$, so the protected subspace here is larger than a reader assuming Frobenius energy would compute.

The general-ability instrument is weak on two of the three models, by the authors' own admission. 'Results on GPT-J and GPT2-XL for GLUE are omitted, as these models exhibit limited GLUE performance prior to editing, making threshold-dependent variations less informative in this setting.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Every general-ability claim — the 62.6% localisation result, the decile-sensitivity result, the 86.34% retention, Figures 9 and 16 — rests on LLaMA3 alone.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The paper prints no aggregate Score in any results table, although Figure 1's own y-axis is labelled 'Score' and the source benchmarks aggregate by harmonic mean.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: [본서 관찰] The aggregate is precisely where a low Neighborhood term becomes visible. Recomputing it (see experiments.note_writer_derived_aggregates) gives MEMIT+REVIVE on GPT-J zsRE = 50.72 at 10,000 sequential edits, against plain MEMIT's printed 50.7 at 10,000 batch edits — i.e. the aggregate the source paper reported is unchanged.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Decimal precision is inconsistent inside Table 1 — 62.3, 54.9, 56.9, 30.5, 4.4, 522.1 appear alongside 55.02, 48.11, 603.22, 31.83 — indicating hand assembly.

The two works the paper cites as questioning the field's evaluation protocol are declined rather than addressed, and one of them is specifically about the metric this paper's specificity claims use: 'Are we evaluating the edit locality of llm model editing properly?' (arXiv:2601.17343).

No code, no data release, no random-seed statement, no layer list, no matrix shapes, no total runtime for the headline experiments. The reproducibility surface is a single runtime table for 100 samples.

The paper discloses LLM assistance in writing and in generating plotting scripts, and the manuscript contains a grammatical error in its central claim sentence ('sequential editing fails when cumulative update progressively corrupt the dominant singular directions').
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Not a defect in itself, but it is the same sentence that carries the paper's thesis, and it sits alongside the swapped figure references and the duplicated Table 4 row.
unfavorable_facts.source: [§2, p.2; 'Usage of large language models', p.9]

LoRA·ROME·MEMIT가 여기 해당한다 ... 3단계에서 읽을 첨자가 없으므로 판정이 성립하지 않는다.' condition_2_budget.verdict: FAILS — and this is the condition that decides
condition_2_budget.reasoning: The strict reading, which is the book's operative one: $\mathrm{gen}(\cdot;B_s)$ is the identity. The content of every write is a human-authored (s,r,o) triple pulled from CounterFact or zsRE in order. No inference over accumulated experience produces what gets written; $B_s$ buys only the arithmetic of writing something already given. ch19 §19.8.4 states this as the gate in so many words — '그 순간 gen(·;B_s)가 항등이 아니게 되고 B_s가 처음으로 조절 가능한 knob이 되며, ch11의 판별식 조건 (2)가 비로소 만족된다' (of SEAL). Nothing in this paper changes that for MEMIT.
condition_2_budget.the_problem_this_exposes: ch11 §11.3's printed 4단계 test is looser: '그 연산자가 추가 추론을 소비하는가. 저장·복사·색인만 한다면 $B_s=0$이고 조건 (2)에서 탈락이다.' By that wording this paper PASSES (2) — MEMIT's $z_i$ optimisation is gradient descent, REVIVE adds a full SVD and two matrix products, and Table 9 prices the whole round at 332.14 s per 100 edits. None of that is 저장·복사·색인. So the book's two statements of condition (2) do not agree, and this paper is the case that separates them. The book must choose: either (2) means 'the budget buys inference' (paper passes) or (2) means 'the budget produces the CONTENT of the write' (paper fails). Only the second reading keeps MEMIT out.

book_impact.verdict_one_line: It does NOT break the Θ ceiling of ch19/ch22, and the focus question's premise about ch22 is mis-aimed. It makes ch19's specificity datum CONDITIONAL in letter while confirming it in substance, it forces a sixth survival condition into ch22 §22.8.4, it threatens ch22's 'KL은 조종간이 아니라 계기판' evaluation by offering a candidate steering wheel, and it strengthens ch22's core verdict by isolating 도달 실패 as the binding constraint.
book_impact.a_what_the_collapse_mechanism_actually_i: The claim '지배적 특이방향 훼손' means: SVD each edited FFN slice; call dominant the top-$k$ by NUCLEAR-NORM SHARE ($\sum\sigma_i$, not $\sum\sigma_i^2$) reaching threshold $\theta_{\mathrm{prot}}$; measure drift with two instruments — $\mathrm{LS}_k$, the Frobenius cosine between the round-0 and round-$k$ low-rank reconstructions, and $\mathrm{SS}^k_j$, the cosine between an edited dominant singular vector and each original one. Supporting claims: top-5% share reconstruction recovers ~62.6% of GLUE [§2.2]; equal-norm perturbations of the 0-20% energy deciles degrade GLUE sharply while 70-100% ones do not [§2.3]; over 20 MEMIT rounds LS falls sharply after ~round 15 and SS reaches near-orthogonality by round 20, tracking behavioural collapse [§2.4]. **The diagnosis is associational** — the paper's own words are 'closely associated' and 'suggesting a primary mechanism' — and the perturbation experiment is close to definitional. **The mitigation is interventional**, which is the stronger half: blocking the drift blocks the collapse [§4.2, App. G.6].
book_impact.b_what_subspace_preservation_costs: Requirements: (i) an SVD of the CURRENT weight slice before every round [App. C.6]; (ii) $c_{ij}=u_i^{\top}\Delta\Theta v_j$ for all $i,j$, i.e. $U^{\top}\Delta\Theta V$ — though the printed Algorithm 1 asks for something $O(m^2n^2)$ and infeasible; (iii) zero every coefficient with $i\le k$ or $j\le k$, i.e. the two-sided projector $(I-U_kU_k^{\top})\Delta\Theta(I-V_kV_k^{\top})$; (iv) one scalar, fixed at 0.10 for every model. **Compute cost**: +4.05% (GPT-J) / +1.91% (LLaMA3) wall-clock per 100 edits [Table 9] — the cheapest Theta-path control in the corpus. **Absolute cost**, never stated: ≈9.2 h / 23.0 h / 46.1 h for 10,000 GPT-J / 10,000 LLaMA3 / 20,000 LLaMA3 edits [본서 산술]. **Memory cost**, never stated: >1.1 GB transient per edited slice per round under PyTorch SVD defaults [본서 산술, shape assumed]. **Quality cost, and this is the real one**: Table 7 shows a monotone frontier — raising $\theta_{\mathrm{prot}}$ from 0.05 to 0.30 moves LLaMA3 Neighborhood 59.70 → 71.86 while Paraphrase falls 86.03 → 67.56, and GPT2-XL Efficacy falls 91.89 → 73.03. Specificity is bought with generalisation, not recovered.
book_impact.c_what_the_20000_edit_number_holds: ONLY the editing metrics on CounterFact and zsRE. Table 6 reports Eff/Para/Neigh/Flu/Consis and zsRE Eff/Para/Neigh for four REVIVE arms and nothing else — no baseline column, no pre-edit row, no aggregate. **General ability is NOT measured at 20,000 edits**; every GLUE/MMLU figure stops at 10,000, where the claim is 86.34% of pre-edit retained. The only 20,000-edit non-editing evidence is a qualitative t-SNE (Fig. 12). **Downstream/generative quality** is represented only by n-gram entropy (Fluency), which at 20,000 edits is 557.61 for MEMIT-REVIVE against a pre-edit 635.47 [본서 관찰 — the paper never makes this comparison]. **Specificity is not held**: CounterFact Neighborhood 89.73 → 56.90, a 32.83-point loss. **Retention by edit recency is not measured at all**, and the evaluation protocol is not even stated (see todo_verify). So the honest one-liner is: 20,000 edits with editing-metric efficacy intact, specificity down a third, fluency down 12%, general ability unmeasured, and early-edit retention unknown.

d_does_ch22_need_rewriting.premise_correction: The focus question asks whether ch22's verdict should move from '쌓을 수 없다' to '기하를 통제하지 않으면 쌓을 수 없다'. ch22 does not carry that verdict. It explicitly declines one — '최종 판정은 하지 않는다. 경로별 판정은 ch27이, 반증 조건의 정식화는 ch30이 소유한다' — and instead issues five survival conditions C1-C5 in §22.8.4. The Θ-path verdict lives in ch27 판정 4 ('조건부로 유망하다'). So the edit this paper forces is to the C-list and to ch27 판정 4's 미검증 clause, not to a ch22 verdict sentence.
d_does_ch22_need_rewriting.the_edit_that_is_required: ch22 §22.8.4 needs a **C6 — 업데이트의 기하를 통제해야 한다.** The existing C-list is derived from one paper and names two prescriptions for 역량 실패 (C2 frozen teacher, C3 proximal term). This paper supplies a third that is mechanism-grounded, orders of magnitude cheaper, works on closed-form editors that have no teacher and no loss to add a penalty to, and is demonstrated at $k=200$ against Continual Facts' $k=100$. Omitting it would leave the C-list incomplete in exactly the way §6.4 forbids.
d_does_ch22_need_rewriting.the_evaluation_that_is_threatened: ch22 §22.6.4 and §22.7 both conclude that the cleanest quantitative law in the falsifier literature is a dashboard, not a steering wheel — '가장 깨끗한 정량 법칙이 조종간이 아니라 계기판이라는 뜻', and 'KL은 배포 카나리아이고 목적함수의 조종간이 아니다' (C3). Those sentences are correct ABOUT KL. But if the book leaves them as written a reader takes away 'no controllable handle for 역량 실패 exists', and this paper contradicts that: constraining the update's spectral support is a handle, it is applied at the update rather than at the objective, and the intervention holds max SS = 1 and 86.34% of GLUE for 10,000 edits. The passage must be narrowed to KL and must name the spectral alternative.
d_does_ch22_need_rewriting.the_verdict_that_is_confirmed_and_streng: ch22 §22.8.3's [평가] — '가중치는 넣을 자리가 없어서 지는 것이 아니라 넣은 것을 부를 이름이 없어서 진다' — survives untouched and gains force. This paper removes 역량 실패 (ii) as a confound out to 20,000 edits and says nothing whatever about 도달 실패 (iii). Critically, its Efficacy and Paraphrase probes SUPPLY THE EDIT PROMPT as a cue, and ch22 §22.6.5 already established that supplying a cue lifts bare-statement strict accuracy from 23% to 99% and collapses the entailment gap from 31.8pp to 0.9pp. **Therefore 91.94% Efficacy at 20,000 edits is a cued probe and must never be read in this book as evidence about reachability.** With (ii) shown fixable and (iii) untouched, (iii) becomes the only live falsifier — which is precisely what ch22 argued.
d_does_ch22_need_rewriting.what_would_actually_change_the_ch22_verd: A table breaking Efficacy down by edit recency at $k=200$, or a composition test over two facts written 10,000 edits apart, or an uncued self-statement probe on an early edit. None exists. The book should add these to ch30 §30.5 as observation types.

what_this_paper_does_NOT_license: It does not license reading 91.94% Efficacy at 20,000 edits as retention or reachability. The evaluation protocol is unstated and the probe is cued.
It does not license 'general abilities are preserved at 20,000 edits'. That was measured at 10,000.
It does not license weakening ch19's zsRE 26.6 < 27.0 caveat. The recomputed aggregate at twice the horizon is 50.72 against 50.7.
It does not license extending anything to fast weights. There is no $W$ in this paper, exactly as in ch22.
It does not license a causal claim about the dominant subspace. The diagnosis is associational; only the mitigation is interventional.
It does not license 'sequential editing is solved'. On the sharp specificity probe the model is 33 points below its pre-edit self, and the paper never makes that comparison.
